title: Duality and Rigidity in Monoidal Categories

items.title: Left dual and right dual object
The zig-zag identities
What 'left' refers to in 'left dual'
A left dual of an object has that object as a right dual
items.strategy: Reflect the left-dual data across the two zig-zag composites to build the mirrored evaluation and coevaluation, then verify the right-dual zig-zags by straightening the same string-diagram composites.

items.title: The unit is self-dual
items.strategy: Take the evaluation and coevaluation to be the unit isomorphism and its inverse, then read the two zig-zag identities as the monoidal triangle identities specialized to the tensor unit.

items.title: Reversing the tensor product exchanges left and right duals
items.strategy: Rewrite the left-dual zig-zags in the reverse monoidal structure and observe that the tensor-order reversal turns them exactly into the right-dual zig-zags, and conversely.

items.title: Duals are unique up to a unique compatible isomorphism
items.strategy: Compose the coevaluation of one dual with the evaluation of the other to define the comparison map, then use the zig-zag identities twice to prove both compatibility and uniqueness.

items.title: Duality yields adjunctions of tensoring functors
items.strategy: Transpose a map across the coevaluation and evaluation of a chosen dual object, prove the two transpose constructions are inverse, and then package them as the unit-counit data for the tensoring adjunctions.

items.title: A dual object in the endofunctor category is an adjoint functor
items.strategy: Read composition of endofunctors as the tensor product and compare the evaluation, coevaluation, and zig-zag identities term by term with the counit, unit, and triangle identities of an adjunction.

items.title: A second proof that adjoints are unique
items.strategy: Apply dual uniqueness inside the endofunctor-composition monoidal category, where left adjoints appear exactly as left duals of the same endofunctor.

items.title: Rigid object and rigid monoidal category
Not every monoidal category is rigid
items.strategy: Use an infinite-dimensional vector space V inside the monoidal category of all vector spaces: if coev(1)=sum v_i tensor f_i were finite, then the zig-zag identity would expand every vector v as a linear combination of the finitely many v_i, contradicting infinite dimension.

items.title: Finite-dimensional vector spaces are rigid
items.strategy: Work in the published monoidal category of modules over a field, choose a finite basis and dual basis, define coevaluation by the finite sum of basis vectors tensor dual basis vectors, and verify the two zig-zag identities by coordinate expansion.

items.title: The dual of a morphism
Left duality is a contravariant antimonoidal functor
items.strategy: Check that the transpose formula for f^vee preserves identities and reverses composition, then use uniqueness of duals together with the reversed tensor order on dual pairs to identify (X tensor Y)^vee with Y^vee tensor X^vee.

items.title: The double dual is a monoidal functor
items.strategy: Compose the contravariant antimonoidal left-duality functor with itself, so the two order reversals cancel and the induced comparison maps assemble into a monoidal endofunctor.

items.title: Left and right duals, and double duals, need not collapse
items.strategy: Follow the source warning that a rigid category can have nontrivial double-dual functors and nonisomorphic left and right duals; the authoring step either supplies one checked witness covering both failures or downgrades this scaffold to a recorded remark rather than inventing a witness.

items.title: In a rigid category every morphism of monoidal functors is an isomorphism
items.strategy: Use rigidity to manufacture candidate inverses to the component on each object by inserting duals and monoidal structure maps, then verify the two composites collapse by the monoidal naturality squares and the zig-zag identities.

items.title: A braided rigid category has a Drinfeld morphism
items.strategy: Build u_X by threading the braiding through the coevaluation and evaluation defining the left and right duals, then prove naturality and invertibility by the hexagon identities together with rigidity.

items.title: The categorical trace of a morphism into the double dual
What is needed before a trace can be written
Pivotal structure
The dimension of an object relative to a pivotal structure
Spherical structure
Pivotal and spherical structures vary by monoidal automorphisms of the identity
In a spherical category the left and right traces agree
items.strategy: Expand the spherical condition through the pivotal comparison maps and rewrite the left and right trace composites until they become the two sides of the source theorem's identity.

items.title: Basic properties of the categorical trace
items.strategy: Compute the left and right traces by functoriality of duality and tensor product, deriving duality, multiplicativity, and double-dual cyclicity directly; in the additive setting, pass through the biproduct decomposition to obtain trace additivity.

items.title: Exact-sequence additivity of trace and its missing hypotheses
Twist and ribbon structure
A twist on a braided rigid category is the same thing as a pivotal structure of Drinfeld type
items.strategy: Starting from a twist theta, compose it with the Drinfeld morphism u_X and verify the monoidal axioms; conversely, solve theta_X from a Drinfeld-type pivotal structure and check the twist equation by expanding u_{X tensor Y}.

items.title: Rigidity alone does not make a tensor category
FALSE: a trace can be defined for an endomorphism in any monoidal category
items.strategy: Refute the claim by isolating the missing comparison V to V double-dual: without rigidity the trace is not even typed, and without a pivotal structure an endomorphism V to V does not become an input to the categorical trace.

items.title: FALSE: a braiding suffices to define a trace
items.strategy: Refute the near-miss by separating the Drinfeld morphism from a pivotal structure: a braiding gives u_X, but only a twist makes u_X theta_X into the monoidal comparison needed to trace endomorphisms.

items.title: FALSE: left and right duals of an object are isomorphic
items.strategy: Use the contingent witness from the noncollapse counterexample: rigid categories can separate left from right dual data even when both exist.

items.title: FALSE: every monoidal category is rigid
items.strategy: Refute the claim with the monoidal category of all vector spaces, where any duality witness for an infinite-dimensional space would force a finite spanning family.

items.title: FALSE: the left and right traces always agree
items.strategy: Refute the claim by pointing to the theorem that equality of the two traces is a spherical, not merely rigid or pivotal, phenomenon.

items.title: FALSE: the dimension of an object is independent of the pivotal structure
items.strategy: Refute the claim by changing a pivotal structure by a nontrivial monoidal automorphism of the identity, which changes the comparison maps whose trace defines the dimension.

title: Duality and Rigidity in Monoidal Categories — Examples

items.title: The dual of a finite-dimensional vector space as a categorical dual
items.strategy: Choose a basis and its dual basis, write the evaluation and coevaluation maps explicitly, and check that they are exactly the categorical duality data for V and V*.

items.title: The zig-zag identities in finite-dimensional vector spaces
items.strategy: Expand the two composites on a basis vector and on a dual basis vector, and observe that both collapse to the identity by the Kronecker-delta evaluation formulas.

items.title: The categorical trace of a linear endomorphism is its matrix trace
items.strategy: Use the canonical finite-dimensional pivotal structure V to V** to turn an endomorphism T into an input of the categorical trace, then evaluate the resulting composite in a basis and recover the sum of diagonal entries.

items.title: The dimension of a vector space is its linear dimension
items.strategy: Trace the canonical pivotal comparison of a finite-dimensional vector space, compute the resulting scalar in a basis, and identify it with the cardinality of that basis.

items.title: An infinite-dimensional vector space has no dual object
items.strategy: Apply the finite-coevaluation spanning argument to a concrete infinite-dimensional space such as k[x] or k^(N): the categorical dual axioms would force a finite spanning family, which the chosen space does not have.

items.title: An adjunction read as a duality of endofunctors
items.strategy: Take the currying adjunction - times A dashv (-)^A in Set and reinterpret its unit and counit as the coevaluation and evaluation exhibiting the exponential functor as a right dual in the endofunctor-composition monoidal category.

items.title: A symmetric monoidal category in which every object is self-dual
items.strategy: Work in finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field: dual bases show V* has the same finite dimension as V, so an isomorphism V to V* exists for each object even though it is not canonical.
